answers.rationale: Maya repeatedly treats included breakfast as useful but secondary to the more reliable workday setup: closer access, stronger reviews, easy dinner, and less morning/evening friction. B is cheaper, closer on foot, higher rated, and has stronger recent room and dining-location feedback; a nearby cafe is an acceptable breakfast workaround.

Maya normally favors nonstop or simpler routing, but she accepts a connection when savings are substantial. Here the $309 gap is unusually large and, more importantly, B stays below the automatic $450 grant reimbursement cap. Its two connections are short but reasonable; D's 6h25 layover is the sort of excessive travel friction she consistently avoids.

Maya repeatedly pays a moderate premium to avoid added connection, transfer, and schedule-risk points on work travel. D is the straightforward one-stop itinerary to the actual destination with a workable connection and ample dinner buffer. A appears cheaper in airfare, but adds an uncertain shuttle or rental-car leg and its ground-transfer cost; B wastes hours in Denver and C adds two tight connections.

A preserves Maya's usual preference for a non-punishing outbound, nonstop travel, and avoiding an unnecessarily late return. It arrives far ahead of the Sunday reception and, with carry-on only, gives a plausible post-panel departure window Wednesday. B requires a very early Sunday start and returns at 2:20 a.m.; C and D add connections without a compensating schedule advantage.
